statement.p: Find the differential of f(x,y) = \sqrt{x^{3}+y^{2}} at the point (2,1).
Then use the differential to estimate f(2.04,0.9).

static.solution:
f_x(x,y) = and f_y(x,y) =, f_x(2,1) = and f_y(2,1) =.
Thus the differential at the point (2,1) is df = df(2,1) = f_x(2,1)\,dx + f_y(2,1)\,dy = 2dx+0.333333dy.
Using the differential at the point (2,1), we can estimate f(2.04,0.9). Since \Delta f \approx f_x(2,1)\Delta x + f_y(2,1)\Delta y, where \Delta f = f(2.04,0.9) - f(2,1) and \Delta x = 2.04 - 2 and \Delta y = 0.9 - 1, we have f(2.04,0.9) \approx f(2,1) + f_x(2,1)(2.04-2) + f_y(2,1)(0.9-1) \approx 3 + \,(0.04) + (-0.1) = 3.04667.
